mainTopic: רבי יוחנן on מום קל and the mixed-looking בכור, the שרוע/שינוי debate, the stories of a גיורת and רב מרי בר רחל on partnership with a גוי, and the משנה exempting כהנים and לויים
overview: This amud opens with two rulings of רבי יוחנן. First, an animal partly owned by a נכרי is exempt from בכורה even if removing the gentile's share would cause only a מום קל. This sides with רב הונא against רב חסדא and רבא. Second, a mixed-looking firstborn (a ewe's goat-like lamb with some of its mother's signs) is a בכור, but its look counts as a מום קבוע. The גמרא asks what this second ruling adds, citing משניות about a pig-like mouth and an eye large like a calf's. It answers that the large eye is a blemish because the animal is a שרוע. It then debates whether the mismatched-eye blemish might still come from שינוי, since two matching eyes have a natural explanation. Next come two stories about partnership with a גוי: רבא tells a גיורת that nobody follows רבי יהודה, and רב מרי בר רחל's animals die after he gave their ears to a גוי. The גמרא gives two explanations for his punishment. Either he removed even the כהן's holiness, or others might copy him without a proper קנין. The amud ends with a new משנה: כהנים and לויים are exempt from פטר חמור by a קל וחומר.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even a part that would cause a slight blemish
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that if a נכרי owns even a part of the animal whose removal would leave only a מום קל, the animal is exempt from בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי יוחנן said: even if removing the gentile's share would cause only a slight blemish, the animal is exempt from the firstborn laws.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports רבי יוחנן's view on how small the gentile's share can be and still exempt the firstborn from קדושת בכורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא discussed an animal co-owned with a נכרי, which is exempt from בכורה. The debate was how big the gentile's share must be. רבי יוחנן says even a tiny share is enough, one whose removal would cause just a מום קל and would not make the animal a נבילה or טריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Partnership with a gentile (the background case)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'slight blemish' here is not about whether the animal is a blemished בכור. It measures how small the gentile's share is: a part whose removal would leave only a minor blemish.

phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even a slight blemish.
phrases.notes: Even if the gentile owns a part whose removal would cause only a minor blemish, the animal is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (on the previous עמוד) about a firstborn partly owned by a gentile.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gentile's share exempts the animal from בכורה even if removing that share would cause only a מום קל.

steps.title: A mixed-looking firstborn counts as having a permanent blemish
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן comments on a משנה about a ewe that bore a goat-like lamb. If the lamb has some of its mother's signs, it is a בכור, but its appearance is a מום קבוע, so it may be slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about the משנה that says a ewe that gave birth to a goat-type, or a goat that gave birth to a ewe-type, is exempt from בכורה, but if the offspring has some of its mother's signs it is obligated: רבי יוחנן said this counts as a permanent blemish, so it may be slaughtered on account of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ruling of רבי יוחנן. He says a firstborn that looks like a different species but keeps some of its mother's features has a built-in permanent blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says such a lamb is holy as a בכור if it has some of its mother's signs. רבי יוחנן adds that its strange appearance is itself a מום קבוע. So it cannot go on the מזבח, and a כהן may slaughter and eat it like any blemished בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: And regarding that which we learned [in a משנה]
To slaughter it on account of [the blemish]

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling becomes the target of the rest of this passage. The גמרא will ask what new information it adds.

phrases.english: And regarding what we learned: a ewe that gave birth to a goat-type
and a goat that gave birth to a ewe-type —
is exempt from the firstborn obligation,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִקְצָת סִימָנִין — חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: and if it has some of the [mother's] signs — it is obligated.
[Rabbi Yochanan said:] It is a permanent blemish,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן's comment on the משנה.

phrases.english: to slaughter it on account of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second statement of רבי יוחנן, attached to the first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור that looks like another species but has some of its mother's signs has a מום קבוע and may be slaughtered.

steps.title: The first ruling clearly teaches something new
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא grants that the first ruling (מום קל) is needed: it shows רבי יוחנן agrees with רב הונא and rejects רב חסדא and רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense why he taught 'a slight blemish': it teaches us that he holds like רב הונא, and excludes the view of רב חסדא and רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its challenge. It first admits that the first ruling has a clear purpose, so it can then ask what the second ruling adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא held that even owning just the ear exempts the animal. רב חסדא and רבא required a share whose removal would make the animal a נבילה or טריפה. רבי יוחנן's 'even a slight blemish' sides with רב הונא, so that ruling is useful.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / It makes sense (opens a 'this part is fine, but...' challenge)

phrases.english: Granted, [the ruling of] a slight blemish —
teaches us [that he holds] like Rav Huna,
and excludes [the view] of Rav Chisda and Rava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts examining whether each of רבי יוחנן's rulings teaches something new, beginning with the first.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether each of רבי יוחנן's statements adds new information.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first does: it takes a side in the רב הונא vs. רב חסדא/רבא debate.

steps.title: What does the permanent-blemish ruling add? A משנה already says it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the second ruling teaches. If it is that a changed appearance is a blemish, a משנה already says a lamb with a mouth like a pig's is blemished.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the 'permanent blemish' ruling, what does it teach us? That since it looks different, it counts as a blemish? We already learned that: if its mouth looks like a pig's, that is a blemish!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's second ruling as unnecessary, because an existing משנה already teaches the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The likely point of the ruling is that an animal with an unusual appearance is considered blemished. But the משנה in the blemish chapter already lists 'a mouth like a pig's' as a מום. So רבי יוחנן seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: We already learned [this in a משנה]

phrases.english: But [the ruling of] a permanent blemish —
what does it teach us?
That since it looks different, it counts as a blemish?
We already learned: 'and its mouth is like that of a pig' —
this is a blemish!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מוּם קָבוּעַ מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The 'but' half of the בשלמא structure, aimed at the second ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that the mixed-looking בכור has a מום קבוע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: the משנה about a pig-like mouth already teaches that a changed appearance is a blemish.

steps.title: Suggested difference: changing into a species that has בכורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a distinction. The pig-mouth case changes toward a species with no קדושת בכורה, while here the lamb changes toward a goat, which does have קדושת בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: there, it changed into something whose species is not holy as a firstborn; here, it changed into something whose species is holy as a firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible defense of רבי יוחנן, explaining why his ruling might still be needed. This is a proposal it will test in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Looking like a pig, an impure animal with no בכורה, is clearly a defect. Looking like a goat, which is itself a valid firstborn species, might not seem like a defect. So רבי יוחנן could be teaching that even this counts as a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible answer)

phrases.english: And if you say: there, it changed
into something whose species is not holy as a firstborn,
[while] here, it changed
into something whose species is holy as a firstborn,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a distinction to answer the redundancy challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps looking like another valid firstborn species would not count as a blemish.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן teaches that even a change toward a species with קדושת בכורה is a מום.

steps.title: That too is in a משנה: one eye large and one small
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggested distinction. A משנה already says that an animal with one large eye and one small eye is blemished. The next step explains why this case already covers a change toward a species that has קדושת בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This too we already learned: its one eye is large and one is small.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the suggested answer by pointing to another משנה that already covers this kind of change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא claims this משנה already covers the distinction from Step 5. As the ברייתא in the next step explains, the large eye is like a calf's eye, and a calf is a species with קדושת בכורה. If that is still a מום, then a change toward a holy species is already known to be a blemish, and רבי יוחנן's ruling seems redundant.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא accepts that רבי יוחנן's מום קל ruling sides with רב הונא. For now, his מום קבוע ruling seems redundant because of two משניות: the pig-like mouth and the mismatched eyes. Step 7 sharpens this challenge, and Step 8 answers it.

phrases.english: This too we have learned:
its one eye is large and one is small.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the distinction offered in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proposed distinction between changing toward a species with or without קדושת בכורה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A משנה already treats one eye large and one small as a blemish. The large eye is like a calf's (Step 7), and a calf is a species with קדושת בכורה, so a change toward a holy species is also already taught.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the large eye is like a calf's eye, which seems to bring the challenge back
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the 'large eye' is as big as a calf's eye. A calf has קדושת בכורה, so the 'other species' distinction fails here too. The only reason left seems to be that a change in appearance is a blemish, so רבי יוחנן's ruling is again unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught: 'large' means as large as a calf's eye, and 'small' means as small as a goose's eye. The goose's eye is fine for the distinction, because geese have no קדושת בכורה. But a calf does have קדושת בכורה! So isn't the reason simply that once the animal's look changed, it counts as a blemish?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that defines the large and small eyes from the משנה in Step 6. It uses that definition to show that change of appearance must be the reason for the blemish, which makes רבי יוחנן's ruling redundant again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 tried to explain רבי יוחנן's ruling: the pig-mouth case changes toward a species with no קדושת בכורה, while his case changes toward a goat, which has it. This ברייתא answers that attempt. A calf's eye comes from a species that does have קדושת בכורה, yet it is still a blemish. So the משנה seems to already teach that any changed appearance is a blemish, even toward a holy species.

keyTerms.meaning: A teacher of the era of the משנה; here, a ברייתא that explains the משנה
Calf, a species that has קדושת בכורה
Goose, a bird with no קדושת בכורה
'Granted…' Admits one part before challenging another

steps.confusionAlert: The calf's eye is not being called a 'goat-like' change. The point is that a calf, like a goat, is a species that has קדושת בכורה. That is why the distinction from Step 5 cannot explain why it is a blemish.

phrases.english: And a tanna taught: 'large' means as large as that of a calf,
and 'small' means as small as that of a goose.
phrases.notes: Defines the 'one large eye and one small eye' from the משנה quoted in Step 6.

phrases.english: Granted, an eye as small as a goose's
has no sanctity of the firstborn in its species,
phrases.notes: So the distinction from Step 5 would work here.

phrases.english: but an eye as large as a calf's —
there is sanctity of the firstborn in its species!
Rather, is it not because we say:
since it changed, it is a blemish?
phrases.notes: If so, רבי יוחנן's second ruling again adds nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּאָמְרִינַן: כֵּיוָן דְּאִישְׁתַּנִּי הָוֵה לֵיהּ מוּמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא to the דחיה of Step 6. It shows that even an eye from a species with קדושת בכורה counts as a blemish.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבי יוחנן's second ruling that a changed appearance is a blemish
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A calf's eye comes from a holy species and is still a blemish. So the משנה already teaches that change of appearance alone is a blemish, and רבי יוחנן's ruling is redundant.

steps.title: The large eye is a blemish because the animal is a שרוע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the calf-sized eye is a blemish for a different reason. The animal has one limb bigger than its pair, which the Torah calls שרוע. It is not because of changed appearance.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is a blemish because the animal is a שרוע, one with a limb bigger than its partner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 7. It gives a different reason why the large eye is a blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שרוע is a blemish listed in the Torah: one limb larger than its matching limb. One huge eye next to a normal eye fits that description. So this משנה does not teach that change of appearance is a blemish, and רבי יוחנן's ruling can still teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with one limb larger than its matching limb, a blemish listed in ויקרא כ״ב

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps רבי יוחנן's ruling meaningful. Whether a changed appearance is a blemish on its own is still a new point that he teaches.

phrases.english: No, it is because it is a 'sarua' (an animal with a limb that is too large).
phrases.notes: The source of this blemish is ויקרא כ״ב:כ״ג.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 7 by giving another reason for the blemish.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the reason behind the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The calf-sized eye is a blemish because the animal's appearance changed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The calf-sized eye is a blemish because one eye is much bigger than the other, which makes the animal a שרוע.

steps.title: Support from a משנה listing extra blemishes that apply only to a person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says its answer makes sense and quotes a משנה. Animal blemishes also disqualify a כהן. A person, though, has extra blemishes, such as both eyes being large or both being small.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense, as we learned in a משנה: these blemishes, whether permanent or temporary, disqualify a כהן. A person has more blemishes than these: both his eyes large, or both his eyes small.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a proof for its answer that the eye is a blemish because of שרוע. Here it only quotes the source. The reasoning comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה puts 'both eyes large or both small' on the list of blemishes found only in a person. That means these are not blemishes in an animal. This detail sets up the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This also makes sense.' Introduces support for the answer just given
A person has more (blemishes) than these, beyond the animal list

phrases.english: This also stands to reason, as we learned in a mishna:
These blemishes,
whether permanent or temporary, disqualify (a כהן).
A person has more than these:
if both his eyes are large, or both are small.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the answer of Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the one-large-eye blemish comes from שרוע
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה listing blemishes found only in a person, including both eyes large or both small

steps.title: Why both eyes large is a blemish only for a person, not an animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that a כהן must look like the rest of זרע אהרן, based on 'איש איש מזרע אהרן'. That rule is only for people. For an animal, both eyes large or both small is not a blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a person it is written 'Any man from the offspring of אהרן', meaning we need a man who looks like the rest of אהרן's offspring. But an animal with both eyes large or both small is not blemished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind the משנה from Step 9. This gives the key fact for the proof: in an animal, both eyes large is not a blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both eyes large or both small is a blemish for a כהן only because of a special verse requiring him to look normal among כהנים. Animals have no such verse. So an animal whose whole look is unusual, with both eyes large, is not blemished.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Any man from the offspring of אהרן' (ויקרא כ״ב:ד)
Equal to (looking like) the rest of אהרן's offspring

phrases.english: It is regarding a person that it is written:
'Any man from the offspring of Aaron,'

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָעֵינַן אִישׁ שָׁוֶה בְּזַרְעוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן,
phrases.english: meaning we require a man who is equal to the seed of Aaron,
phrases.notes: He must look ordinary, like other כהנים.

phrases.english: but an animal,
if both (eyes) are large or both are small —
it is also not a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה from Step 9 and draws from it the rule for animals.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the one-large-eye blemish comes from שרוע
steps.raayaSupportSource: The verse 'איש איש מזרע אהרן', which limits the both-eyes blemish to a person

steps.title: So one large eye must be a blemish because of שרוע, not because of change
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its proof. Both eyes large is not a blemish in an animal, even though that also changes how it looks. So the blemish of one large eye cannot come from change. It must come from שרוע.
steps.simpleTranslation: So when one eye is large and one is small, why is it a blemish? If it were because of change in appearance, then both eyes large or both small should be a blemish too! Rather, isn't it because the animal is a שרוע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the proof that started in Step 9, arguing for the answer of Step 8: the mismatched-eye blemish comes from שרוע. The next step will reject this proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If change of appearance were the reason, an animal with both eyes large would also be blemished, since it also looks different. Step 10 showed that it is not. So the only difference is that one eye does not match the other, which is שרוע. This means the משנה never taught that change alone is a blemish, and רבי יוחנן's ruling is not redundant.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, is it not…?' A rhetorical question that pushes to a conclusion

steps.whatToRemember: The proof argues that a mismatched eye is a blemish because of שרוע, since an animal with both eyes large is not blemished. Steps 12–13 push back: a mismatch can still be a שינוי, because two matching eyes have a natural explanation.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not treat this proof as final. Step 12 answers that the mismatch itself can count as a שינוי, because two matching eyes have a natural explanation.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof held, the משנה about one large eye would not teach that change of appearance is a blemish, and רבי יוחנן's ruling would stay a new teaching. The next step challenges the proof.

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת גְּדוֹלָה וְאַחַת קְטַנָּה, מַאי טַעְמָא?
phrases.english: One large and one small, what is the reason (it is a blemish)?
If it is because of change (in appearance) —

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ שְׁתֵּיהֶן גְּדוֹלוֹת, שְׁתֵּיהֶן קְטַנּוֹת נָמֵי!
phrases.english: then even both large or both small should also be a blemish!
Rather, is it not because it is a 'sarua'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ שָׂרוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rule from Step 10 to complete the proof for the answer of Step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Proposed proof (rejected in Steps 12–13): the one-large-eye blemish is based on שרוע, not on change of appearance.

steps.title: No, the blemish really is because of changed appearance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from steps 9–11. It says one large eye is a מום because of שינוי, and שינוי really is a blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, I can really tell you that it is because of the change, and a change is a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof it just built. It says the blemish of one large eye can still come from שינוי after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 concluded that the blemish must come from שרוע, because both eyes large is not a blemish even though it also looks different. Now the גמרא says no: שינוי really is the reason. It still owes us an answer about the two-large-eyes case, and it gives that in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: No, really — the formula for rejecting a proof and going back to the original idea
A change or difference in how the animal looks

phrases.english: No, really I will tell you
it is because of the change,
a change is a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion of step 11, which said the blemish comes from שרוע and not from שינוי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof (steps 9–11) that one large eye cannot be a blemish because of שינוי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that two large eyes are also a שינוי. The next step shows they are not.

steps.title: Why two big eyes or two small eyes are not a change
steps.stepSummary: Two large eyes can come from extra health, and two small eyes can come from extra weakness. Only a mismatched pair is a real שינוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for what bothered you — that even if both are big or both are small it should be a blemish — there, if the big eye came from extra health, both eyes should have been healthy. If the small eye came from extra weakness, both eyes should have been weak.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question that seemed to break the שינוי explanation. It explains why two matching eyes are not considered a change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Big eyes can come naturally from a very healthy animal, and small eyes from a weak one. But health and weakness affect the whole body evenly. So when only one eye is big or small, there is no natural explanation, and that mismatch is the real שינוי that makes it a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: And as for what bothered you — the formula for going back to answer an earlier difficulty

steps.whatToRemember: The proof for שרוע is deflected. One mismatched eye can be a מום because of שינוי, while two matching eyes are not a שינוי, since health or weakness would explain them.

phrases.english: And as for what is difficult for you:
even if both are big,
or both are small, it should be a blemish?
There, if the big eye were from extra health —
phrases.notes: Very healthy animals naturally have large eyes.

phrases.english: both eyes should have been healthy,
if the small eye were from extra weakness —
both eyes should have been weak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection in step 12 by answering the two-eyes question from step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any unusual eye size, including two big eyes, counts as a שינוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a mismatch between the two eyes is a שינוי. Matching eyes have a natural explanation.

steps.title: רבא's ruling for a convert who fattened animals with her gentile brothers
steps.stepSummary: A גיורת raised animals for her gentile brothers in a partnership. רבא told her that nobody worries about רבי יהודה's view that שותפות גוי is חייבת בבכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain convert whose brothers would give her animals to fatten. She came before רבא. He said to her: Nobody is concerned for this view of רבי יהודה, who said that a partnership with a גוי is obligated in בכורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic and tells a story. A גיורת asks רבא whether firstborn animals in her partnership with gentiles are a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her brothers were still gentiles, so the animals were partly owned by a גוי. רבי יהודה holds that such animals still get קדושת בכורה. רבא rules that הלכה does not follow him, so her firstborn animals are exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: To fatten them, usually for a share of the profit
Nobody is concerned for it — meaning halacha does not follow this view
Partnership with a non-Jew in owning an animal
The holiness and laws of a firstborn animal

phrases.english: There was a certain female convert
whose brothers would hand over to her
animals to fatten,
she came before Rava,
he said to her: There is no one who is concerned
for this view of Rabbi Yehuda, who said:
partnership with a gentile is obligated in firstborn status.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא גִּיּוֹרְתָּא דַּהֲווֹ מָסְרִין לַהּ אַחֵי חֵיוְתָא לְפַטּוֹמַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to the earlier argument about שותפות גוי in בכורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה. An animal partly owned by a גוי is exempt from בכורה.

steps.title: רב מרי בר רחל gave the animals' ears to a gentile, and the animals died
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי בר רחל gave a גוי ownership of the ears of his firstborn animals. He still did not shear them or work them, and he gave them to כהנים. His animals died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי בר רחל had a certain flock. He would transfer ownership of their ears to a גוי. He forbade shearing them and working them, and he gave them to the כהנים. And the animals of רב מרי בר רחל died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story about a גוי's partnership. This story sets up the questions in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because a גוי owned a part of the animal (its ears), the animal would not get קדושת בכורה. Even so, רב מרי treated the animals like a real בכור in every practical way. The story ends with his animals dying, which hints that he did something wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Shearing and working the animal, both forbidden with a בכור

phrases.english: Rav Mari bar Rachel
had a certain flock of animals,
he would transfer ownership of their ears to a gentile,
phrases.notes: This refers to the firstborn while still unborn, so that they would be born without firstborn holiness.

phrases.english: but he prohibited them from shearing and labor,
and gave them to the priests,

phrases.aramaic: וּכְלַאי חֵיוָתָא דְּרַב מָרִי בַּר רָחֵל.
phrases.english: and the animals of Rav Mari bar Rachel died.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מָרִי בַּר רָחֵל הַוְיָא לֵיהּ הָהִיא חֵיוָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story about a גוי's partial ownership removing קדושת בכורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ownership by a גוי of even one part, like the ears, removes קדושת בכורה.

steps.title: Why give the ears to a gentile if he treated them as holy anyway?
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי kept all the בכור rules. So the גמרא asks why he bothered to give the ears to a גוי at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since he forbade shearing and working them, and gave them to the כהנים, why did he transfer ownership of their ears to a גוי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב מרי's behavior. It seems to contradict itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he was going to treat the animals as a בכור anyway, removing their holiness gained him nothing. It also seems wrong to take away holiness for no reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Since — introduces the facts the question is built on

phrases.english: But since he prohibited them
from shearing and labor,
and gave them to the priests,
why did he transfer ownership of their ears to a gentile?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּאָסַר לְהוּ בְּגִיזָה וַעֲבוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the logic of רב מרי's actions described in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מרי's practice of giving the ears to a גוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Removing the holiness seems pointless if he kept every בכור rule anyway.

steps.title: He wanted to protect the כהנים from sinning
steps.stepSummary: He removed the holiness so that if the כהנים sheared or worked the animals by mistake, they would not be doing an איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Lest they come to a mishap with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why רב מרי gave the ears to a גוי. It was a safety net.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He still treated the animals as holy and gave them to כהנים. But the כהנים might shear or work them, and that is forbidden with a real בכור. Since the animals were not truly holy, any such slip would not be a sin.

keyTerms.meaning: A mishap, meaning stumbling into a sin

phrases.english: Lest they come to a mishap with them.
phrases.notes: The fear is that the כהנים might shear or work the animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Giving the ears to a גוי served no purpose.
steps.terutzMaskana: It protected the כהנים from accidentally sinning with a real בכור.

steps.title: Then why were his animals punished?
steps.stepSummary: If רב מרי had a good reason, the גמרא asks why his animals died.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the reason that the animals of רב מרי died?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If he meant well, why was he punished?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 made his act look like a good thing. But the story said his animals died, which looks like a punishment. So something about what he did must have been wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: If so — introduces a challenge to the previous answer

phrases.english: If so, what is the reason
that the animals of Rav Mari died?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מַאי טַעְמָא כְּלוֹ חֵיוָתָא דְּרַב מָרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 17 using the ending of the story in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that his intention was good
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A good act should not be punished, yet his animals died.

steps.title: He was punished for removing the animals' holiness
steps.stepSummary: His animals died because he took away their קדושה, even though his reason was good.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he removed them from their holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final answer: the problem was taking away the קדושה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A good intention does not make it right to cancel the holiness the Torah gives a בכור. Removing that holiness was itself wrong, and that is why he was punished.
steps.whatToRemember: Giving a גוי part ownership of an animal can remove קדושת בכורה. But doing this on purpose is looked down on, even with a good reason, because it cancels holiness.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that something can work in הלכה and still be improper. Using a loophole to avoid קדושה is frowned upon.

phrases.english: Because he removed them from their sanctity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18. Step 20 challenges this answer, and step 22 offers an alternative.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Removing קדושת בכורה on purpose is wrong, even when it is done for a good reason.

steps.title: רב יהודה allows blemishing a firstborn before birth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 19 with רב יהודה's ruling that it is permitted to put a מום on a בכור before it is born.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב יהודה say that a person may put a blemish on a firstborn animal before it comes out into the world?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. If removing holiness is so bad, why does רב יהודה let a person put a מום on a בכור before it is born?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 said רב מרי was punished for taking away the animal's קדושה. But putting a מום on an unborn בכור also takes away some of its holiness, and רב יהודה says this is allowed. So removing holiness before birth seems fine, and רב מרי should not have been punished.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [he] say? (introduces a contradicting source)
A blemish that makes an animal unfit for the מזבח
To put a blemish on an animal
Into the air of the world, meaning being born

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda say:
it is permitted for a person to put a blemish on a firstborn
phrases.notes: This means a firstborn animal still inside its mother.

phrases.english: before it comes out into the air of the world!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 19's claim that removing קדושה caused the punishment
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that רב מרי was punished for removing his animals' קדושה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יהודה permits removing sanctity before birth by putting a מום on it. So removing sanctity before birth should not be blameworthy.

steps.title: A blemish removes only altar holiness, not the כהן's holiness
steps.stepSummary: A מום removes only קדושת מזבח, and the animal still goes to the כהן. רב מרי's sale removed even קדושת כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, he only removes the animal's altar holiness. He does not remove its priestly holiness. Here, רב מרי removed even its priestly holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two cases are different. A blemish takes away less holiness than what רב מרי did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished בכור cannot be brought on the מזבח, but it still belongs to the כהן. That is a partial loss. When רב מרי gave a גוי a share in the ears, the animal lost its בכור status completely, so the כהן lost his right to it. That full removal is what was punished.

keyTerms.meaning: Altar holiness: fit to be brought as a קרבן
Priestly holiness: must be given to a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: A בכור has two levels of holiness. A מום removes only the altar level. Giving a גוי a share removes both levels.

phrases.english: There, from the sanctity of the altar
he removes it,
from the sanctity of the priest he does not remove it.
phrases.notes: The blemished בכור is still given to the כהן.

phrases.english: Here, even from the sanctity of the priest
he removes it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם מִקְּדוּשַּׁת מִזְבֵּחַ קָא מַפְקַע לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20 by distinguishing the cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any removal of holiness before birth is allowed, as with a מום
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a partial removal (altar holiness) is allowed. Removing the כהן's holiness too is what caused the punishment.

steps.title: Others might copy רב מרי without doing it properly
steps.stepSummary: A second reason for the punishment: רב מרי knew how to make a complete sale, but others watching him might do it wrong and come to sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you could say: רב מרי בר רחל knew how to make a complete transfer of ownership. But another person sees him, goes and does the same, and thinks it is the same thing רב מרי did. Then he stumbles into a sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different reason why רב מרי's animals died. The problem is not what he did, but what others might do when they copy him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here, removing holiness itself is not the problem. The danger is that an onlooker will not make a real, complete קנין. His animal stays a true בכור, but he treats it as ordinary and shears or works it. רב מרי was held responsible for creating that risk.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces an alternative answer)
A complete, legally valid transfer of ownership
A mishap, stumbling into a sin

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not say רב מרי's own sale failed. It worked for him. The worry is only about other people who see him and copy him badly.
steps.whatToRemember: Two reasons for רב מרי's punishment: (1) he removed even the כהן's holiness, or (2) others might copy him without a proper קנין and come to sin.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Rav Mari bar Rachel knew
how to transfer ownership with a complete transaction,
and another person sees him,
and goes and does it (without a complete transaction),

phrases.aramaic: וְסָבַר רַב מָרִי מִילְּתָא הוּא דַּעֲבַד,
phrases.english: and thinks: Rav Mari did this same thing,
and he comes through it to a mishap.
phrases.notes: He would treat a real בכור as ordinary, for example by shearing or working it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent answer to the question of Step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative reason (concern that others will be misled)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The punishment was for removing the animal's holiness
steps.terutzMaskana: The punishment was because onlookers might copy him without a proper קנין and come to sin
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A respected person must avoid actions that others may imitate incorrectly and come to sin.

steps.title: כהנים and לויים are exempt, learned by a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: New משנה: כהנים and לויים are exempt from redeeming a firstborn donkey (פטר חמור), learned through a קל וחומר from the desert.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: כהנים and לויים are exempt, through a קל וחומר. If they exempted the firstborns of ישראל in the desert, it makes sense that they should exempt their own.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules that כהנים and לויים do not have to redeem their firstborn donkeys, and it gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the desert, the לויים and their animals took the place of the firstborns of ישראל, which freed the ישראל firstborns from their status. If the לויים could free other people's firstborns, then they surely free their own. That is the קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lesser case to a greater one
A firstborn donkey, which normally must be redeemed with a sheep

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new topic: who is included in the מצוה of פטר חמור. The גמרא will next examine this קל וחומר.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Priests and Levites are exempt,
phrases.notes: Exempt from redeeming a firstborn donkey.

phrases.english: from an a fortiori argument:

phrases.aramaic: אִם פָּטְרוּ אֶת שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּמִּדְבָּר,
phrases.english: If they exempted those of the Israelites in the wilderness,
phrases.notes: The לויים replaced the firstborns of ישראל (במדבר ג:מה).

phrases.aramaic: דִּין הוּא שֶׁיִּפְטְרוּ אֶת שֶׁל עַצְמָן.
phrases.english: it is logical that they should exempt their own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the רב מרי discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים and לויים are exempt from פטר חמור, derived by a קל וחומר from their exempting ישראל's firstborns in the desert
